34|# Browser Automation with agent-browser
35|
36|When a dev server is running or the user asks to verify, test, or interact with a web page, use `agent-browser` to automate the browser.
37|
38|## Core Workflow
39|
40|Every browser automation follows this pattern:
41|
42|1. **Navigate**: `agent-browser open <url>`
43|2. **Snapshot**: `agent-browser snapshot -i` (get element refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
44|3. **Interact**: Use refs to click, fill, select
45|4. **Re-snapshot**: After navigation or DOM changes, get fresh refs
46|
47|```bash
48|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000
49|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
50|agent-browser snapshot -i
51|```
52|
53|## Dev Server Verification
54|
55|When a dev server starts, use agent-browser to verify it's working:
56|
57|```bash
58|# After starting a dev server (next dev, vite, etc.)
59|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000
60|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
61|agent-browser screenshot dev-check.png
62|agent-browser snapshot -i
63|```
64|
65|## Command Chaining
66|
67|Commands can be chained with `&&`. The browser persists between commands via a background daemon.
68|
69|```bash
70|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000 && agent-browser wait --load networkidle && agent-browser snapshot -i
71|```
72|
73|## Essential Commands
74|
75|```bash
76|# Navigation
77|agent-browser open <url>              # Navigate (aliases: goto, navigate)
78|agent-browser close                   # Close browser
79|
80|# Snapshot
81|agent-browser snapshot -i             # Interactive elements with refs
82|agent-browser snapshot -i -C          # Include cursor-interactive elements
83|agent-browser snapshot -s "#selector" # Scope to CSS selector
84|
85|# Interaction (use @refs from snapshot)
86|agent-browser click @e1               # Click element
87|agent-browser fill @e2 "text"         # Clear and type text
88|agent-browser type @e2 "text"         # Type without clearing
89|agent-browser select @e1 "option"     # Select dropdown option
90|agent-browser check @e1               # Check checkbox
91|agent-browser press Enter             # Press key
92|agent-browser scroll down 500         # Scroll page
93|
94|# Get information
95|agent-browser get text @e1            # Get element text
96|agent-browser get url                 # Get current URL
97|agent-browser get title               # Get page title
98|
99|# Wait
100|agent-browser wait @e1                # Wait for element
101|agent-browser wait --load networkidle # Wait for network idle
102|agent-browser wait --url "**/page"    # Wait for URL pattern
103|agent-browser wait 2000               # Wait milliseconds
104|
105|# Capture
106|agent-browser screenshot              # Screenshot to temp dir
107|agent-browser screenshot --full       # Full page screenshot
108|agent-browser screenshot --annotate   # Annotated screenshot with numbered labels
109|agent-browser pdf output.pdf          # Save as PDF
110|
111|# Diff (compare page states)
112|agent-browser diff snapshot           # Compare current vs last snapshot
113|agent-browser diff screenshot --baseline before.png  # Visual pixel diff
114|```
115|
116|## Common Patterns
117|
118|### Form Submission
119|
120|```bash
121|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/signup
122|agent-browser snapshot -i
123|agent-browser fill @e1 "Jane Doe"
124|agent-browser fill @e2 "jane@example.com"
125|agent-browser click @e5
126|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
127|```
128|
129|### Authentication with State Persistence
130|
131|```bash
132|# Login once and save state
133|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/login
134|agent-browser snapshot -i
135|agent-browser fill @e1 "$USERNAME"
136|agent-browser fill @e2 "$PASSWORD"
137|agent-browser click @e3
138|agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"
139|agent-browser state save auth.json
140|
141|# Reuse in future sessions
142|agent-browser state load auth.json
143|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/dashboard
144|```
145|
146|### Data Extraction
147|
148|```bash
149|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/products
150|agent-browser snapshot -i
151|agent-browser get text @e5
152|agent-browser get text body > page.txt
153|```
154|
155|### Visual Debugging
156|
157|```bash
158|agent-browser --headed open http://localhost:3000
159|agent-browser highlight @e1
160|agent-browser record start demo.webm
161|```
162|
163|## Ref Lifecycle (Important)
164|
165|Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, etc.) are invalidated when the page changes. Always re-snapshot after:
166|
167|- Clicking links or buttons that navigate
168|- Form submissions
169|- Dynamic content loading (dropdowns, modals)
170|
171|```bash
172|agent-browser click @e5              # Navigates to new page
173|agent-browser snapshot -i            # MUST re-snapshot
174|agent-browser click @e1              # Use new refs
175|```
176|
177|## Annotated Screenshots (Vision Mode)
178|
179|Use `--annotate` for screenshots with numbered labels on interactive elements:
180|
181|```bash
182|agent-browser screenshot --annotate
183|# Output: [1] @e1 button "Submit", [2] @e2 link "Home", ...
184|agent-browser click @e2
185|```
186|
187|## Semantic Locators (Alternative to Refs)
188|
189|```bash
190|agent-browser find text "Sign In" click
191|agent-browser find label "Email" fill "user@test.com"
192|agent-browser find role button click --name "Submit"
193|```
194|
195|## JavaScript Evaluation
196|
197|```bash
198|# Simple expressions
199|agent-browser eval 'document.title'
200|
201|# Complex JS: use --stdin with heredoc
202|agent-browser eval --stdin <<'EVALEOF'
203|JSON.stringify(
204|  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("img"))
205|    .filter(i => !i.alt)
206|    .map(i => ({ src: i.src.split("/").pop(), width: i.width }))
207|)
208|EVALEOF
209|```
210|
211|## Session Management
212|
213|```bash
214|agent-browser --session site1 open http://localhost:3000
215|agent-browser --session site2 open http://localhost:3001
216|agent-browser session list
217|agent-browser close  # Always close when done
218|```
219|
220|## Timeouts and Slow Pages
221|
222|```bash
223|agent-browser wait --load networkidle  # Best for slow pages
224|agent-browser wait "#content"          # Wait for specific element
225|agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"  # Wait for URL pattern
226|agent-browser wait 5000                # Fixed wait (last resort)
227|```

43|2. **Snapshot**: `agent-browser snapshot -i` (get element refs like `@e1`, `@e2`)
44|3. **Interact**: Use refs to click, fill, select
45|4. **Re-snapshot**: After navigation or DOM changes, get fresh refs
46|
47|```bash
48|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000
49|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
50|agent-browser snapshot -i
51|```
52|
53|## Dev Server Verification
54|
55|When a dev server starts, use agent-browser to verify it's working:
56|
57|```bash
58|# After starting a dev server (next dev, vite, etc.)
59|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000
60|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
61|agent-browser screenshot dev-check.png
62|agent-browser snapshot -i
63|```
64|
65|## Command Chaining
66|
67|Commands can be chained with `&&`. The browser persists between commands via a background daemon.
68|
69|```bash
70|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000 && agent-browser wait --load networkidle && agent-browser snapshot -i
71|```
72|
73|## Essential Commands
74|
75|```bash
76|# Navigation
77|agent-browser open <url>              # Navigate (aliases: goto, navigate)
78|agent-browser close                   # Close browser
79|
80|# Snapshot
81|agent-browser snapshot -i             # Interactive elements with refs
82|agent-browser snapshot -i -C          # Include cursor-interactive elements
83|agent-browser snapshot -s "#selector" # Scope to CSS selector
84|
85|# Interaction (use @refs from snapshot)
86|agent-browser click @e1               # Click element
87|agent-browser fill @e2 "text"         # Clear and type text
88|agent-browser type @e2 "text"         # Type without clearing
89|agent-browser select @e1 "option"     # Select dropdown option
90|agent-browser check @e1               # Check checkbox
91|agent-browser press Enter             # Press key
92|agent-browser scroll down 500         # Scroll page
93|
94|# Get information
95|agent-browser get text @e1            # Get element text
96|agent-browser get url                 # Get current URL
97|agent-browser get title               # Get page title
98|
99|# Wait
100|agent-browser wait @e1                # Wait for element
101|agent-browser wait --load networkidle # Wait for network idle
102|agent-browser wait --url "**/page"    # Wait for URL pattern
103|agent-browser wait 2000               # Wait milliseconds
104|
105|# Capture
106|agent-browser screenshot              # Screenshot to temp dir
107|agent-browser screenshot --full       # Full page screenshot
108|agent-browser screenshot --annotate   # Annotated screenshot with numbered labels
109|agent-browser pdf output.pdf          # Save as PDF
110|
111|# Diff (compare page states)
112|agent-browser diff snapshot           # Compare current vs last snapshot
113|agent-browser diff screenshot --baseline before.png  # Visual pixel diff
114|```
115|
116|## Common Patterns
117|
118|### Form Submission
119|
120|```bash
121|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/signup
122|agent-browser snapshot -i
123|agent-browser fill @e1 "Jane Doe"
124|agent-browser fill @e2 "jane@example.com"
125|agent-browser click @e5
126|agent-browser wait --load networkidle
127|```
128|
129|### Authentication with State Persistence
130|
131|```bash
132|# Login once and save state
133|agent-browser open http://localhost:3000/login
134|agent-browser snapshot -i
135|agent-browser fill @e1 "$USERNAME"
136|agent-browser fill @e2 "$PASSWORD"
137|agent-browser click @e3
138|agent-browser wait --url "**/dashboard"

144|```
145|

162|
163|## Ref Lifecycle (Important)
164|
165|Refs (`@e1`, `@e2`, etc.) are invalidated when the page changes. Always re-snapshot after:

178|
179|Use `--annotate` for screenshots with numbered labels on interactive elements:
180|
181|```bash

187|## Semantic Locators (Alternative to Refs)
188|
189|```bash

193|```

195|## JavaScript Evaluation
196|
197|```bash

200|
201|# Complex JS: use --stdin with heredoc
202|agent-browser eval --stdin <<'EVALEOF'
203|JSON.stringify(
204|  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("img"))
205|    .filter(i => !i.alt)
206|    .map(i => ({ src: i.src.split("/").pop(), width: i.width }))
207|)
208|EVALEOF
209|```

217|agent-browser close  # Always close when done

# jomaa-static-pages

Static websites and the hub's web device panel. Standalone sites are served at
their own hostnames through the hub's Cloudflare tunnel on jerry.

| Folder | Hostname |
|--------|----------|
| `sarah.jomaa.org/` | https://sarah.jomaa.org |

## Device panel

`device-panel/` contains the web light controller at
https://jomaa.org/lights. It controls rooms with power, brightness, white
temperature, and color settings, and shares the hub's administrator sign-in.
The session stays signed in until it expires.

The screen fills the viewport from top to bottom:

- The top row shows the room name on the left and a dot for each device on
  the right: green when the device answered, red when it failed or is
  unreachable, and yellow after a command until that device reaches the
  requested state. Short notes such as "1 of 2 on" or "last known" sit beside
  the dots.
- A round power button glows with the light's color or white temperature at
  its brightness.
- The remaining height is split evenly between 10/50/75/100% brightness
  presets, a warm-to-cool temperature track, and red, orange, and two custom
  color circles. Each control fills its band.
- With more than one room, the bottom edge is a T split with one half per
  room (Living Room and Bedroom). Without rooms, it lists devices.

The pencil on a custom circle opens a grid of colors; picking one saves it in
the browser and applies it. After a command the panel re-reads the hub about
once a second until every device confirms or ten seconds pass, then names
devices that didn't get there. It also re-reads the hub when it becomes
visible and every minute.

The hub serves this panel with its API. `jomaa-home-hub/scripts/build-web.mjs`
copies the panel and its styles into the hub build. Run
`npm run build` from `jomaa-home-hub/` after editing the panel. Changes to this
folder trigger hub verification and deployment through GitHub Actions.
The panel is part of the hub build and does not need a static site route.

```
browser ── https ──▶ Cloudflare ── tunnel ──▶ jerry: serve.py on 127.0.0.1:8090
                                               picks the hostname directory by Host
```

`serve.py` serves files only (no directory listings, no hidden files) to
hostnames discovered from its directory names, and answers 404 for anything else.
`/healthz` returns the server's health independently of the site hostname.

## Edit the portfolio

Each artwork is one entry in `sarah.jomaa.org/artworks.js`. Put the image in
`sarah.jomaa.org/images/` and add an entry with its title, year, medium, size,
series and pixel width and height. The series filter buttons come from the
`series` values. The current images are generated sample art; swap them for
real photos or scans (JPEG or WebP, about 2000 px on the long side). Replace
the contact address `sarah@example.com` in `index.html`.

Preview locally:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8765 --directory jomaa-static-pages/sarah.jomaa.org
```

## Publish and add sites

Verified pushes to `main` discover hostname directories, deploy their files,
restart the static server, and create the tunnel routes and DNS records.

To publish `new.jomaa.org`, add its files under:

```text
jomaa-static-pages/new.jomaa.org/index.html
jomaa-static-pages/new.jomaa.org/gallery/index.html
```

Push the new directory to `main`. Folder names define the hostnames, and each
site's files define its URL paths. The example also publishes
`https://new.jomaa.org/gallery/`. Removing a hostname directory removes its
public route and managed DNS record at the next deployment.

The static server and deployer use the same directory discovery. Hostname
directories require an `index.html`. Support folders such as `device-panel/`
are excluded. See [`../jomaa-deploy/README.md`](../jomaa-deploy/README.md) for
receiver installation and infrastructure configuration.

```bash
systemctl --user status jomaa-static-pages
journalctl --user -u jomaa-static-pages -f
```

## Test

```bash
cd jomaa-static-pages && python3 -m unittest test_static_pages -v
```

event.text: Balancing concise verdict with detailed review structure while separating live UI inspection from isolated stub provenance and avoiding real-state claims.
Balancing concise verdict with detailed review structure while separating live UI inspection from isolated stub provenance and avoiding real-state claims.

**Verdict:** Strong phone-first remote — one screen, no scroll, big thumb targets — but it's a room remote, not a light panel: coarse, room-only control with a few state displays that ask you to guess.

I checked the live sign-in at `jomaa.org/lights` and exercised the signed-in panel rendered from [app.js](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/app.js:806) against an isolated stub hub, so no physical lights were touched. Screenshots are in `/tmp/lights-ux/`.

**What works**

The power circle is the whole design and it lands: it glows with the current temperature/color and brightness, so on/off is readable across a room. The one-viewport layout in [style.css](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/style.css:108), `44px` tap floor, focus rings, `aria-live` announcer, and reduced-motion support are all solid. Feedback is honest: commands apply optimistically, then [confirm()](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/app.js:726) re-reads for up to 10s, dots go yellow while pending, and failures name the devices. Capability-based hiding also works — the Bedroom view correctly dropped the color row.

**Friction, biggest first**

No individual lights once rooms exist. [buildTabs()](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/app.js:781) lists rooms only, so one lamp in a 10-lamp room is unreachable from here. That also contradicts the docs in [jomaa-home-hub/README.md](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-home-hub/README.md:99), which promise individual devices, a top picker, both-rooms selection, and a Refresh button — none exist; refresh is only the 60s/visibility auto-refresh in [app.js](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/app.js:1083).

Brightness is four presets (10/50/75/100) with no slider, and mixed rooms show none selected because [summarize()](/home/danieljomaa/jomaa-everything/jomaa-static-pages/device-panel/app.js:372) only reads lit devices. The main color row is just red, orange, and two customs; the full palette hides behind a tiny pencil badge, and picking there both saves and immediately fires the color, so you can't preset it for later.

State reads ambiguously in places. The dots mean reachable, not on — a dark lamp still shows green, with identity only in a hover tooltip. The temperature slider has no visible value, just Warm/Cool ends. When a color is active the temperature band dims but stays enabled, and when everything is off the temperature gradient stays fully vivid even though touching it turns the lights on; neither behavior is discoverable.

Layout is phone-only in practice. On desktop the bands stretch full-width with dead space around the `30dvh` power circle, and when a room lacks color the remaining two bands inflate to fill the height, so Bedroom looks noticeably emptier than Living Room.

**Minor:** no sign-out, no link back to `/home`, `/devices`, or `/manage`, and three names for one page — `/lights`, "Device Panel", "Hub password". Worth aligning the docs either way: ship the missing picker/multi-select, or rewrite that README section to match the simpler room-only panel.
